subject: Social Habits
title: Staying safe at school
objectives: Children will stay with their group and an adult.
Children will say stop or hot for dangerous things.
content: Staying with my teacher, hot, sharp and dirty things, and safe play.
teachingActivities: Keep rules few and clear; use the words stop, hot and wait; practise rules by play; praise safe behaviour; never frighten children; check the compound for hazards daily; keep gates secure and count children often.
learnerActivities: Stay with the group and an adult and stop when told stop.
resources: A hot sign with a picture of a hot pot
Pictures of safe and unsafe play
assessment: Observe whether each child stays with the group and stops when told stop.
expectedOutcomes: Stays with the teacher in the compound.

lessons.title: Staying with my teacher
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will stay with their teacher and group.
successCriteria: Holds a rope or a hand when walking
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines and use the toilet with support.
lessons.starter: Sing "Stay with me, stay with me, hold the rope and walk with me."
teacherActivities: Show how to hold a loop of the rope.
Walk slowly around the room together.
Say "We always stay with our teacher."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hold a loop of the rope. Children: Children hold a loop.
Step 2. Teacher: Walk slowly around the room together. Children: Children walk with the rope.
Step 3. Teacher: Stop and count the children. Children: Children stand still and look.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We always stay with our teacher." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Rope walk
steps: Hold a loop of the rope.
practical.safety: Walk slowly and keep a second adult at the back of the line. Use soft rope with loops and never tie children to it.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand at the front of the line.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to help count the group.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Stays with the teacher and group
Walks with a rope or hand
lessons.conclusion: Sit together and count the children.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise staying close and holding hands in public places.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "stay with their teacher and group" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Stay with me, stay with me, hold the rope and walk with me.

lessons.title: Stop and hot
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will stop when they hear stop and say hot for dangerous things.
successCriteria: Says hot for a hot picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines and use the toilet with support.
lessons.starter: Hold up the stop sign and say "When I say stop, we stop still like a statue."
teacherActivities: Play stop and go with music.
Show the hot sign and say "Hot! Do not touch."
Show pictures of sharp or dirty things and say "Ask a grown-up."
learnerActivities: Children say hot and step back.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play stop and go with music. Children: Children move and stop.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the hot sign and say "Hot! Do not touch." Children: Children say hot and step back.
Step 3. Teacher: Show pictures of sharp or dirty things and say "Ask a grown-up." Children: Children say no touch.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise children who stop quickly. Children: Children smile and clap.

practical.title: Stop game
steps: Stop when the teacher says stop.
Say hot to a hot picture.
practical.safety: Use only pictures of hot and sharp objects, never real ones. Keep the floor clear and stop movement games quickly if a child is hurt.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and stop together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a hot thing in a picture.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do when we hear stop?
Is a hot pot safe to touch?

lessons.conclusion: Stand still like a statue and then wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Teach hot and stop at home with a pretend game.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "stop when they hear stop and say hot for dangerous things" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Safe play outdoors
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will play safely outdoors with an adult watching.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines and use the toilet with support.
resources: A play area marked with cones or a rope
lessons.starter: Show the play area boundary and say "We play inside the rope where it is safe."
teacherActivities: Show the boundary and how to play inside it.
Let children play with the equipment.
Ring the bell and say "Come back."
Say "We play safely and look after friends."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the boundary and how to play inside it. Children: Children walk around the boundary.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children play with the equipment. Children: Children play safely.
Step 3. Teacher: Ring the bell and say "Come back." Children: Children come to the teacher.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We play safely and look after friends." Children: Children repeat safe.

practical.title: Safe play
practical.safety: Check the area for hazards before play and keep an adult at every piece of equipment. Never leave children unattended.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child and stay close.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to remind a friend to stay inside.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do at the bell?

lessons.conclusion: Count the children and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play in safe places at home and set clear limits.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play safely outdoors with an adult watching" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Safe and unsafe pictures
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will sort pictures into safe and unsafe.
successCriteria: Says no for an unsafe picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines and use the toilet with support.
resources: Pictures of safe and unsafe actions
Two baskets: smiling face and stop sign
lessons.starter: Show two baskets and say "Safe things go in the happy basket. Unsafe things go in the stop basket."
teacherActivities: Show a picture and ask "Is it safe?"
Put the picture in the correct basket.
Talk about why one is unsafe.
learnerActivities: Children look and say yes or no.
Child puts the picture in a basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a picture and ask "Is it safe?" Children: Children look and say yes or no.
Step 2. Teacher: Put the picture in the correct basket. Children: Child puts the picture in a basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Talk about why one is unsafe. Children: Children point to the danger.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We always stay safe." Children: Children repeat safe.

practical.title: Safe sort
practical.safety: Use only gentle pictures with no frightening images. Stop if a child becomes worried and comfort them.

differentiation.support: Offer two pictures and say safe or not first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another unsafe picture.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say to danger?

expectedOutcomes: Sorts pictures into safe and unsafe
lessons.conclusion: Put the baskets away and say "Stay safe."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about safe and unsafe things around the house.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort pictures into safe and unsafe" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 safety check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child follows safety rules.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines and use the toilet with support.
lessons.starter: Sing the safety song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: rope walk, stop game and safe pictures.
At each station watch how the child follows the rule.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: rope walk, stop game and safe pictures. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child follows the rule. Children: Child follows with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Safety stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use only pictures and soft equipment.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to lead the rope walk.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: stays with the group; stops on the word stop; says hot; plays safely.

questions.question: What do we do at stop?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
lessons.conclusion: Count the children and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep safety rules clear and simple at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child follows safety rules" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
